entries.market_reading: In credit analysis 'debt' means interest-bearing borrowings (bank loans, commercial paper, notes and bonds, and usually finance leases), not all liabilities: payables, accruals and deferred revenue are excluded. figures.notes: Fallbacks are components some filers tag instead of the total; add only those not already inside a tagged total.

figures.name: current debt
figures.notes: DebtCurrent is itself the total of the current parts and includes current lease obligations (FASB 2026), while LongTermDebtNoncurrent excludes them, so DebtCurrent + LongTermDebtNoncurrent mixes bases. For a lease-excluded total use LongTermDebtCurrent + ShortTermBorrowings (+ CommercialPaper only when it is not inside ShortTermBorrowings). Never add FinanceLeaseLiabilityCurrent to DebtCurrent, and do not add LongTermDebtCurrent or ShortTermBorrowings to it. us-gaap:LineOfCredit is the current plus noncurrent drawn balance (FASB 2026), not a current component: never add it together with LongTermLineOfCredit. | element notes: us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent + us-gaap:ShortTermBorrowings + us-gaap:CommercialPaper ; us-gaap:NotesPayableCurrent (when presented separately)

figures.notes: LongTermDebt includes the current portion; LongTermDebtNoncurrent excludes it. LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations is noncurrent only (FASB 2026: 'classified as noncurrent'). It leaves out current maturities and short-term borrowings, so it is not a total-debt fallback. If it is the only tag, add LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsCurrent plus any short-term borrowings and name each part. The ...IncludingCurrentMaturities element includes the current portion. DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations covers short-term and long-term debt. All three include lease obligations, so the finance-lease choice must be stated (LS-09). us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount is labelled 'Long-Term Debt, Gross' (FASB 2026): before unamortized discount, premium and debt issuance costs, and often tagged per instrument; never mix it with carrying-amount totals.

notes: How the market reads this family: nearly every liquidity, leverage and coverage ratio is called 'low' or 'high' comparatively, against the company's own 3-5 year history and its industry; the Federal Reserve itself reads aggregate leverage and interest coverage against their own history. Authoritative lines exist only of three kinds: (a) definitional arithmetic (a ratio below 1 means one side exceeds the other; negative equity; interest not covered), (b) events whose direction is in their definition (uncured default under S-X 4-08(c), 8-K Items 1.03 and 2.04, going-concern doubt), and (c) lines a named source draws for its own purpose (bank capital rules 12 CFR 324.10/.403/.12, the LCR minimum 12 CFR 249.10, NAIC RBC bands, S&P's rating bands, Altman's sample zones, the 2013 leveraged-lending 6x line now withdrawn by the OCC and FDIC). Present (c) with its source and purpose, never as a market law. The 12-month horizon is source-drawn: S-K 303(b)(1) defines short-term liquidity as the next 12 months, and ASC 205-40 evaluates going concern one year after issuance (AS 2415: one year after the balance-sheet date). Financial companies (banks, insurers, broker-dealers, many REITs and utilities) present unclassified balance sheets and carry deposits or policy liabilities: corporate current ratios and debt/EBITDA do not apply; route banks to LS-31/LS-32 and insurers to LS-33. Builder findings from the repo: interest_coverage is EBITDA / interest, while the Fed and most investor speech mean EBIT / interest; the interest_expense fallback chain ends at InterestPaidNet (cash paid), mixing accrual and cash bases; the cash fallback CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents includes restricted cash and flatters net debt; net_debt deducts cash only (no marketable securities). Each is a labelling or composition decision for the metric owner, recorded here, not changed. Element names in 'figures' were checked on 2026-09-24 against FASB's 2026 US GAAP taxonomy with the siglia-xbrl-element skill. Absent in 2026: DebtInstrumentDebtDefaultAmount, LineOfCreditFacilityExpirationDate (use...ExpirationDate1), CommonEquityTierOneCapitalToRiskWeightedAssets (use CommonEquityTierOneCapitalRatio), SalesRevenueNet. Deprecated 2026: CapitalLeaseObligations, OperatingLeasesFutureMinimumPaymentsDue(Current). InterestExpense's 2026 label is 'Interest Expense, Operating and Nonoperating'. dei elements were not verifiable by the skill. Element names are identifiers (licence OD); no FASB label or documentation text is stored here. Series breaks a builder must know: Item 503(d) ratio of earnings to fixed charges and Exhibit 12 eliminated effective 5 Nov 2018 (83 FR 50148); the Item 303(a)(5) contractual obligations table eliminated for fiscal years ending on or after 9 Aug 2021 (86 FR 2080); ASC 842 brought operating leases on balance sheet from 2019; ASU 2015-03 (issuance costs net against debt) and ASU 2020-06 (convertibles) changed debt carrying amounts; the community bank leverage ratio fell from 9% to 8% (91 FR 22989, 29 Apr 2026); the OCC and FDIC withdrew from the 2013 leveraged lending guidance on 5 Dec 2025. Mechanics: pair instants with instants at the same date; build trailing twelve months from 10-Q year-to-date values; never add a reported total to its own parts or dimensional members to the undimensioned total; MD&A, covenant, liquidity and contractual-obligation disclosures are passages, not XBRL facts. The absence of a default, going-concern or bankruptcy event never argues that a company is healthy. Altman (2000) was read from the Internet Archive's copy because the NYU host returned HTTP 500; S&P's Corporate Methodology was read from S&P Global Ratings Maalot's published copy.
